# nish/net/http-server

One handler for HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 (over TLS and cleartext) and HTTP/3, with Alt-Svc advertising the HTTP/3 port.

```ts
import {
  HttpServer,
  HttpServerLimits,
  HttpServerRequest,
} from "nish/net/http-server";
```

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
const server = new HttpServer(new HttpServerLimits(), router)
server.listenHttp1(tcpFd, new Http1Config(), 256)
server.listenHttp2Tls(tlsFd, tlsConfig, new Http2Config(), 64)
server.listenHttp3(udpFd, quicConfig, new Http3Config(), 64, entropy)
for (;;) {
  server.waitSigned(1000, key)
  while (server.ready()) {
    const r: HttpServerRequest = server.take()
    if (r.route === HELLO) {
      server.send(r, 200, TEXT_PLAIN, HELLO_BODY, 0, HELLO_BODY.length)
    } else {
      server.refuse(r)
    }
  }
}
```

</scalar-code-group>

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="Http​Server" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#httpserver">

One handler for HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 over TLS and HTTP/3: configure up to one listener of each kind, then loop on `waitSigned` (or `wait`), `ready` and `take`, answering each request with `send`, `json` and `sendJson`, `problem`, `refuse`, or `start`, `write` and `end`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="Http​Server​Limits" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#httpserverlimits">

The caps an `HttpServer` holds itself to; every listener's carrier is checked against them.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="Http​Server​Request" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#httpserverrequest">

One request, whole, from any version: its head copied out of the carrier and its body.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

<scalar-callout type="info">

`HttpServer` is `HttpHandler`'s pull loop (`nish/net/handler`) over up to
four listeners at once. The program builds a `Router`, configures the
listeners, and loops on `waitSigned` (or `wait`, when every listener is
cleartext), `ready` and `take`, switching on `r.route`; one route body
answers every version.

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="One copy in">

Every version copies the request head once into the
request's own `head`, a buffer of `limits.maxHead` bytes made on the
request's first use and never grown: each listen call checks that no head
its carrier accepts can overrun it. The body is held whole, up to
`limits.maxBody`; past it the request is answered 413 on every version.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="A fixed pool">

`limits.requests` requests are shared by every listener.
With none free, an HTTP/1.1 connection stops being read until one is, an
HTTP/2 stream is refused with REFUSED_STREAM and an HTTP/3 one with
H3_REQUEST_REJECTED, so the client may retry. No connection holds more
than a quarter of the pool.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Alt-Svc">

Once an HTTP/3 listener is configured, every HTTP/1.1 and
HTTP/2 over TLS response names its port (`h3=":443"; ma=86400`); with
`altSvcMaxAge` 0 they say `alt-svc: clear` instead. A response whose fields
already hold an `alt-svc` keeps the program's. An h2c response carries
none: it reaches clients through a proxy, and would name the backend's port.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="One HTTP/2 slot space">

The TLS and the cleartext HTTP/2 carriers share
the stream tables: each listener's slots follow the other's, so every
HTTP/2 path below names a slot of either and the carrier is looked up once,
in the `h2Holds` family.

</scalar-detail>

## Classes

### HttpServer

One handler for HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 over TLS and HTTP/3: configure up to one
listener of each kind, then loop on `waitSigned` (or `wait`), `ready` and
`take`, answering each request with `send`, `json` and `sendJson`,
`problem`, `refuse`, or `start`, `write` and `end`.

```ts
class HttpServer
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new HttpServer(limits: HttpServerLimits, router: Router)` | A server routing through `router`, held to `limits`. It has no listener yet: add them with `listenHttp1`, `listenHttp2Tls` and `listenHttp3`. Panics on a limit outside its range. |
| `scratch: u8[]` | `json` and `problem` write here. |
| `connections(): i32` | How many connections are open, of every version. |
| `drain(): void` | Begins a graceful stop: the server accepts no more connections, closes each idle HTTP/1.1 connection now and each other one once its request is answered, and sends GOAWAY on each HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 connection, which then closes once its streams are done. A request already read is still handed over and answered. The listeners are the program's to close. |
| `empty(r: HttpServerRequest, status: i32): i32` | Answers `r` with `status` and no body. |
| `end(r: HttpServerRequest): i32` | Ends `r`'s response. `r` is the server's again: it goes back once the carrier has taken every byte. Panics on another server's request, when the response is not started, or its body is short of the declared length. |
| `fired(id: i32): boolean` | Whether watched descriptor `id` was ready in the last turn. |
| `hungUp(r: HttpServerRequest): boolean` | Whether the client of `r` has hung up: its connection is closed or reused, its HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 stream was reset, or, on HTTP/1.1, the peer ended its side while `r` is held. Panics on another server's request. |
| `json(): JsonWriter` | The JSON writer, reset onto the server's scratch buffer: write one value with it, then `sendJson`. One JSON body at a time, since every request shares the buffer. |
| `listenH2c(fd: i32, config: Http2Config, slots: i32): void` | Serves cleartext HTTP/2 (h2c, prior knowledge: no Upgrade from HTTP/1.1) on `fd`, a listening TCP socket the program made, with up to `slots` connections. Meant for a server behind a TLS-terminating proxy or on a trusted network: nothing on it is encrypted. A connection that has not sent its 24-byte preface within `limits.prefaceTimeout` is closed, and one with no open stream after it within `limits.idleTimeout`. Its responses carry no Alt-Svc, and its requests say `secure` false. Each connection holds at most `config.maxStreams` requests and a quarter of `limits.requests`, as on `listenHttp2Tls`. Panics on a second h2c listener, a `maxHeaderListSize` past `limits.maxHead`, or `enableConnectProtocol`. `wait` serves it: it reads no key. |
| `listenHttp1(fd: i32, config: Http1Config, slots: i32): void` | Serves HTTP/1.1 on `fd`, a listening TCP socket the program made, with up to `slots` connections. Panics on a second HTTP/1.1 listener, or when `config` would let in a head past `limits.maxHead` (its `maxTarget`, its `maxHeaderBytes` and 44 bytes of request line) or more fields than `limits.maxFields`. `config.maxBody` is set to `limits.maxBody`. |
| `listenHttp2Tls(fd: i32, tls: TlsServerConfig, config: Http2Config, slots: i32): void` | Serves HTTP/2 over TLS (ALPN `h2`) on `fd`, a listening TCP socket the program made, with up to `slots` connections. Each connection holds at most `config.maxStreams` requests and a quarter of `limits.requests`; a stream past that is refused with REFUSED_STREAM. Panics on a second listener of this kind, a `maxHeaderListSize` past `limits.maxHead`, or `enableConnectProtocol`. Serve it with `waitSigned`. |
| `listenHttp3(fd: i32, quic: QuicServerConfig, config: Http3Config, slots: i32, entropy: u8[]): void` | Serves HTTP/3 on `fd`, a bound UDP socket the program made, with up to `slots` QUIC connections, and from then on names its port in an Alt-Svc field on every HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 response. Each connection holds at most `quic.maxStreamsBidi` requests and a quarter of `limits.requests`; a stream past that is rejected with H3_REQUEST_REJECTED. Panics on a second HTTP/3 listener, a `maxFieldSectionSize` past `limits.maxHead`, or `webtransportSessions` above 0. Serve it with `waitSigned`. |
| `problem(r: HttpServerRequest, status: i32, title: string, detail: string): i32` | Answers `r` with an RFC 9457 problem: `application/problem+json` with `type` `about:blank`, `title`, `status` and, when not empty, `detail`. Nothing of the request is echoed. |
| `ready(): boolean` | Whether a whole request is waiting for `take`. Requests whose connection or stream closed while queued are handed back here. |
| `refuse(r: HttpServerRequest): i32` | Answers a request the router refused, by its `route`: 405 with an `Allow` field naming the methods the path has, and 404 for anything else. |
| `send(r: HttpServerRequest, status: i32, contentType: u8[], body: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): i32` | Answers `r` with `status`, a `Content-Type` of `contentType` and the body `body[off .. off + len)`, in one call. |
| `sendFields(r: HttpServerRequest, status: i32, names: u8[][], values: u8[][], body: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): i32` | Answers `r` with `status`, the fields `names[k]`: `values[k]` and the body `body[off .. off + len)`, in one call. |
| `sendJson(r: HttpServerRequest, status: i32): i32` | Answers `r` with `status` and the value `json`'s writer holds, as `application/json`. A value the writer refused or did not finish is answered as a 500 problem instead. Panics when no value was begun with `json`. |
| `start(r: HttpServerRequest, status: i32, names: u8[][], values: u8[][], bodyLength: i32): i32` | Starts `r`'s response: `status` (200 to 599), the fields `names[k]`: `values[k]`, and a body of `bodyLength` bytes or `HTTP1_CHUNKED` for one of unknown length; then `write` the body and `end`. On HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 the field names must be lowercase, and a `content-length` is added for a known length the fields do not give; on HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 the Alt-Svc field is added when an HTTP/3 listener is set and the fields have none. Panics on another server's request, a request not taken or already answered, a status outside the range, a body length below `HTTP1_CHUNKED`, or fields the carrier refuses. |
| `take(): HttpServerRequest` | The next whole request, of any version, which the program now owes an answer. Panics when none is `ready`. |
| `wait(timeoutMs: i32): i32` | One turn of the loop for a server with no TLS or QUIC listener: as `waitSigned`, with no key. It serves HTTP/1.1 and h2c (`listenH2c`). Panics when an HTTP/2 over TLS or HTTP/3 listener is configured, since a handshake there needs the key. |
| `waitSigned(timeoutMs: i32, key: Secret<u8[]>): i32` | One turn of the loop: waits up to `timeoutMs` (-1 for no limit) for a socket to be ready, accepts, reads and writes what is, signs each TLS and QUIC handshake with `key`, closes what is past its timeouts, and answers how many whole requests are waiting for `take`. |
| `watch(fd: i32, id: i32): void` | Adds `fd` to the descriptors `wait` and `waitSigned` block on, as `id`: `fired(id)` then says whether it was readable in the last turn. For a program's own descriptors, such as `signalFd()` for a graceful stop. Panics on an id outside 0 to `HANDLER_MAX_WATCHED - 1`. |
| `write(r: HttpServerRequest, buf: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): i32` | Writes `buf[off .. off + len)` of `r`'s body. What the carrier has no room for is copied and sent as room comes, so `buf` is the caller's again on return. Body bytes of a HEAD, 204 or 304 response are dropped. Panics on another server's request, when the response is not started, on a window outside `buf`, or on more bytes than the declared length leaves. |

### HttpServerLimits

The caps an `HttpServer` holds itself to; every listener's carrier is checked against them.

```ts
class HttpServerLimits
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new HttpServerLimits()` |  |
| `altSvcMaxAge: i32` | Seconds a client may remember the Alt-Svc advertisement; 0 sends `alt-svc: clear`. |
| `altSvcPort: i32` | The port Alt-Svc names; 0 names the HTTP/3 socket's own. |
| `bodyTimeout: i32` | Milliseconds from a request's head to the end of its body. |
| `idleTimeout: i32` | Milliseconds an HTTP/2 connection (over TLS or h2c) with no open stream is kept. |
| `jsonBytes: i32` | Bytes in the JSON scratch buffer. At least 256. |
| `maxBody: i32` | The largest request body, in bytes; past it a request is answered 413. 0 to 2^30. |
| `maxEvents: i32` | The most readiness events one `wait` takes. |
| `maxFields: i32` | The most fields a request may carry. 1 to 1024. |
| `maxHead: i32` | The largest request head (method, target and fields), in bytes. 256 to 2^20. |
| `maxResponseFields: i32` | The most fields a response may carry, Alt-Svc and content-length included. 2 to 256. |
| `prefaceTimeout: i32` | Milliseconds a cleartext HTTP/2 connection (`listenH2c`) has to send its 24-byte preface; after it, `idleTimeout` applies. |
| `requests: i32` | The most requests held at once, across every connection and version. 1 to 65536. |

### HttpServerRequest

One request, whole, from any version: its head copied out of the carrier
and its body. Every position is an offset into `head` or `body`, which are
the request's own and stay valid until it is answered.

```ts
class HttpServerRequest
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new HttpServerRequest(index: i32)` | An empty request for the server's pool; its buffers are made on its first use. |
| `body: u8[]` | The body, `body[0 .. bodyLength)`. |
| `bodyLength: i32` | How many bytes of `body` are the request's body, 0 for none; read the body as `body[0 .. bodyLength)`. |
| `head: u8[]` | The method, the target and the header section (field names lowercased); on HTTP/2 and 3, `:authority` is the field `host`. |
| `index: i32` | Its index in the server's pool. |
| `methodEnd: i32` | Where the method ends in `head`, one past its last byte. |
| `methodStart: i32` | Where the method starts in `head`; the method is `head[methodStart .. methodEnd)`. |
| `queryValueEnd: i32` | Where the raw value `queryIndex` found ends in `head`, one past its last byte; it starts at `queryValueStart`. |
| `queryValueStart: i32` | The span `queryIndex` found, raw. |
| `route: i32` | The index `Router.add` answered for the route, or a negative `ROUTER_*` code. |
| `secure: boolean` | Whether it came over TLS or QUIC: true on HTTP/2 over TLS and on HTTP/3. |
| `slot: i32` | The connection's slot in its carrier. |
| `targetEnd: i32` | Where the request target ends in `head`, one past its last byte. |
| `targetStart: i32` | Where the request target (path and query) starts in `head`; the target is `head[targetStart .. targetEnd)`. |
| `version: i32` | The HTTP version it came in on: 1, 2 or 3. |
| `hasQuery(name: string): boolean` | Whether the query holds a parameter named `name`. |
| `header(name: string): i32` | The index of the first field named `name`, which is lowercase, or `HANDLER_ABSENT`. |
| `headerIs(name: string, value: string): boolean` | Whether the first field named `name` (lowercase) has exactly the value `value`. |
| `methodIs(method: string): boolean` | Whether the method is exactly `method` (methods are case-sensitive, RFC 9110 §9.1). |
| `param(k: i32, out: u8[]): i32` | Parameter `k` percent-decoded into `out` from 0 (`routerDecode`): its length, `ROUTER_BAD_ESCAPE` for a malformed escape, or `ROUTER_NO_ROOM` when `out` is too short. Nothing is written on a code. |
| `paramDecimal(k: i32): i32` | Parameter `k` read as a decimal number that is not negative and fits an `i32`, or -1. |
| `paramEnd(k: i32): i32` | Where parameter `k` ends in `head`. |
| `paramIs(k: i32, text: string): boolean` | Whether parameter `k`, raw, is exactly `text`. |
| `paramStart(k: i32): i32` | Where parameter `k` starts in `head`. Panics on a parameter the route does not have. |
| `pathIs(path: string): boolean` | Whether the path, the target up to its `?`, is exactly `path`. |
| `query(name: string, out: u8[]): i32` | The first query parameter named `name`, its value decoded into `out` from 0 — `+` as a space and `%XX` as its byte, the form encoding (application/x-www-form-urlencoded) — and its length; a name is compared decoded too. `HANDLER_ABSENT` when no parameter has the name, `ROUTER_BAD_ESCAPE` for a malformed escape in its value, `ROUTER_NO_ROOM` when `out` is too short. A name with no `=` has an empty value. |
| `queryIndex(name: string): i32` | Finds the first parameter named `name`: where its pair starts, or -1; its raw value goes to `queryValue...`. |
| `valueEnd(i: i32): i32` | Where field `i`'s value ends in `head`. |
| `valueStart(i: i32): i32` | Where field `i`'s value starts in `head`. |
